name: Single-module world (start here)
solution: One database holds world, players and economy. Shard only when load tests show the region ceiling.
tradeoffs: Simple; caps at one core's capacity (~hundreds of active players).

name: Global + region shards
problem: World needs more than one database's capacity.
solution: Root/global database owns accounts, chat, economy ledger, region directory; region databases own spatial simulation. Clients connect to global + current region.
tradeoffs: Cross-region ops become async protocols; ops overhead.

name: Region handoff state machine
problem: Moving a player between databases without dupes/loss.
solution: lock (source marks player in_transit) -> offer (outbox/IDC to target with snapshot + request id) -> accept (target inserts inactive copy, acks) -> delete (source removes) -> activate (target enables, client switches subscription). Every step idempotent keyed by transfer id; timeouts roll back to source.
tradeoffs: Latency of 2 round trips; needs reconciliation sweeper.

name: Fixed-rate tick with budget and auto-throttle
solution: Scheduled tick reducer (e.g. 10-20 Hz) measures its own duration, writes tick_health (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red), and sheds optional work (AI frequency, far entities) when over budget.
tradeoffs: Requires tuning; tick_health adds a small write per tick.

name: Chunk/cell AOI subscriptions
problem: Clients must see nearby world only.
solution: Partition world into cells; entities store cell_x/cell_y (indexed); client subscribes to its 3x3 (or radius) cells, diffing cell sets on movement; tier subscriptions (near: full rows/high rate; far: summary table).
tradeoffs: Cell boundary churn; choose cell size ~ view radius / 1-2.

name: Narrow hot table + wide cold table
solution: Split entity_transform (id, cell, x, y, rot, ts) from entity_info (name, stats, appearance). High-rate subscriptions only touch the narrow table.

name: Entity-component tables
problem: Flexible game objects without wide nullable rows.
solution: entity(id) + one table per component (health, inventory_slot, ai_state) keyed by entity_id; systems iterate component tables.
tradeoffs: More tables/indexes; great for subscriptions by component.

name: Descriptor tables with generation stamps
solution: item_desc/recipe_desc tables reloaded by stage_* reducers into a new generation, then sweep_* removes old generation; clients key caches by generation.

name: Progressive actions
problem: Crafting/harvesting take time and must survive disconnects.
solution: progressive_action row (actor, kind, started_at, completes_at, target); a scheduled reducer completes or cancels; client shows a progress bar from timestamps.

name: Off-tick native sidecar
problem: Heavy compute (pathfinding, mob AI) doesn't fit the tick budget.
solution: A native process connects as a service identity via the SDK, subscribes to what it needs, computes, and commits results through reducers that check the caller is the registered service identity.
tradeoffs: Extra process to deploy; results are one tick late.

name: Deterministic seeded procgen
problem: World generation must match across server, tools and tests.
solution: Hash (seed, x, y, salt) with FNV-1a into a splitmix64 stream; port noise functions bit-exactly and test with golden values.
tradeoffs: Floating point must be handled carefully across languages.

name: Identity broker for third-party auth
solution: Use an OIDC issuer (SpacetimeAuth or Firebase/Auth0 via a token broker issuing RS256 JWTs); map ctx.sender() -> account row on first connect; keep provider ids in a private table.
used_in: template Firebase broker, Godot SDK Steam guide

name: Server-side admission
solution: allowlist table + check in client_connected and every reducer; operator grants are idempotent reducers callable only by an admin identity.
tradeoffs: Every reducer pays a lookup (cheap, indexed).

name: Additive-only migrations + backfill
solution: Only add tables/columns-with-defaults; backfill in batches via a scheduled migration reducer; record schema_version; never rely on init.

name: Server-authoritative combat sub-tick
problem: Fair combat at modest tick rates.
solution: Clients send timestamped intents; server orders them inside the tick by timestamp (clamped to tick window) and resolves hits against server state; clients predict and reconcile.

name: Client SDK seam
problem: SDK upgrades/forks ripple through gameplay code.
solution: One autoload/service owns the connection; exposes typed signals and intent methods; everything else reads the cache.

name: Load-test gate
solution: Headless bot clients (SDK) drive scripted sessions; a monitor polls tick_health/metrics; budgets.json defines p95 limits and must_plateau for memory; output PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL and block publish on FAIL.

name: Outbox + idempotent consumer
solution: Write intents to an insert-only outbox table (2.14 IDC) or a pending_jobs table drained by a procedure/sidecar; consumers dedup by message id.

name: Leaderboards / matchmaking / hidden info via official how-tos
solution: Follow official how-to recipes: top-100 leaderboard, matchmaking queue, skill-based MM, turn-based, sync nearby entities, hide information, seasonal reset.

name: Heightmap terrain chunks
solution: terrain_chunk(cx, cy, heights bytes, version); edits patch bytes in a reducer; clients subscribe by chunk cell and rebuild meshes on update.

name: Ops: pinned side-by-side runtimes
solution: Install versions side by side, run candidate on another port against a copied data dir, run acceptance + two-identity tests, then switch; keep rollback binary and data copy.
